issue.title: Mesh raycaster copy: land the GPU results without waiting for the GPU (U2 iSubMesh assertion)
issue.body:
Uncharted 2 stopped with `ASSERTION: iSubMesh < m_numSubMeshInstances` (`GetSubMeshInstance`, ndlib/render/ngen/mesh.h:1361), usually just after a checkpoint save. It is one of the most reported crashes since 0.3.4 (#9, #37, #43, #47 and several newer ones). This fixes it for the 1.02 builds I could test, without a wait for the GPU.

What the game does: a ray cast against the level's static meshes runs on the GPU, and `MeshRaycaster::HandleResults` reads the hits from a 64-byte record array in the game's own memory. Each hit names a mesh instance and a submesh. The records get there through the 64-dword compute copy shader the port already special-cases, in two steps: GPU output to a staging buffer, then staging buffer to the record array. GPU readbacks are relaxed by default, so a guest read of the record array never fetches GPU data. With the second step copied on the GPU alone, what the game read did not always belong to that copy: the records were plausible hits, but one named submesh 5 of a mesh instance that has 4 submeshes, and the game asserted.

The second step (the copy whose destination the guest CPU writes) now also copies in guest memory, with the GPU-written bytes of its source. The first step's destination is GPU-only, so it is left alone. The shader hash is shared by all three games, there are 7 or 8 raycasters, and each copies about 7 times a second, so the way the bytes get there matters:

- Earlier versions of this PR read the source back at the dispatch. That submits the open command buffer and waits for the whole queue: 40 to 60 waits a second, 19 to 29 percent of the GPU command thread's time in the scenes below (thanks to @adrianeira for pointing at the cost of readbacks).
- Now the dispatch copies the guest part and hands the GPU-written bytes to a landing thread (`BufferCache::DeferGuestCopy`). It waits for the tick of the work that wrote them, copies them on the side queue and writes them into the destination in guest memory. The game learns that the GPU is past the copy from the labels the port writes (end of pipe, end of shader, flip), and it reads the record array as soon as its label shows. So those labels wait for the copy to land (`landing_gate.h`): the deferred ones run on the landing thread behind it, in order, and write data and compute releases wait for it. A real GPU's labels do not show before its work is done either. No thread waits for the GPU at the copy any more.

`BB_SCALAR_COPY64_DEFER=0` goes back to the wait at the dispatch (the previous version of this PR), `BB_SCALAR_COPY64_SYNC=0` turns the fix off, `=1` reads back both steps. Without a side queue the wait at the dispatch is used.

Cost, same build, `BB_SCALAR_COPY64_DEFER=0` against the default, two runs side by side in each scene (60 s, CHEAP render, a PC that was also running other game instances, so the absolute numbers are inflated). "GPU thread blocked" is the share of the time the thread that records and submits spent waiting for GPU ticks (the frame statistics):

| scene | wait at the dispatch: waits/s, ms/s | GPU thread blocked | now | FPS, wait -> now (p99 frame ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U2 gompa (tunnel with Flynn) | 60, 283 | 21.5% | 0.0% | 60.0 -> 59.6 (22.1 -> 17.6) |
| U2 convoy-turret | 60, 208 | 19.0% | 0.0% | 59.8 -> 59.3 (23.4 -> 20.7) |
| U3 tail-sully | 38, 310 | 29.4% | 0.0% | 38.1 -> 52.5 (38.0 -> 33.9) |
| U1 chase, pre-river-bed | 54, 281 | 23.7% | 0.0% | 53.6 -> 59.3 (34.2 -> 17.6) |

The landing thread itself waits for the GPU 190 to 390 ms a second, off the command thread. The 60 FPS scenes stay at about 60; the heavier U3 and U1 scenes are where the GPU thread's wait was costing frames. Labels that follow a raycaster copy show about one GPU latency (a few ms) later than before, as they would on a console.

How often the assertion happens depends on how far the GPU lags the game. About 1 run in 12 on a quiet PC. I raised it with `BB_SUBMIT_DELAY_US=8000` (the GPU thread starts each submission 8 ms late) and a dev menu jump to `gompa-main-buddha-base-zipline-post` on a fresh game instance each time, 40 s of scripted input:

| | runs | assertion |
|---|---|---|
| fix off (`BB_SCALAR_COPY64_SYNC=0`) | 8 | 5 (one more run crashed with the unrelated read fault 0xc04403) |
| wait at the dispatch (previous version) | 33 | 0 |
| this version | 24 | 0 |

These runs are on our integration build, which has the same logic on top of other open PRs. The branch of this PR itself I booted to gameplay in all three games (continue from the title, 40 s each, no assertion or fault); the dev menu jump the repro needs works with a pad token that origin/main builds do not have, so the repro on this exact tree I did not run.

I did not find out exactly which write produces the wrong record. Judging merged GPU data per dword instead of per 64-byte block did not fix it (3 of 4 still asserted without the read back). A trap on the pages of the record array, to land the bytes when the game first touches them, did not work: the game reads the array within about 0.2 ms of the copy and touches the pages around it all the time, so it only moved the wait to the game's threads. What the game reads right after is its label, which is why the labels wait.

Not covered: guest-visible writes that are not one of these packets (a DMA data write used as a fence) do not wait for the copy. I tested on the US 1.02 build only.

comment.body: Reworked this PR again: the wait for the GPU at the dispatch is gone. The dispatch copies the guest part of the record array and a landing thread writes the GPU-written bytes into it once the GPU has made them; the labels the game reads (end of pipe, end of shader, flip) wait for that, so the game still reads the records the copy made. Side by side with the old behaviour (wait at the dispatch), the GPU command thread's blocked share goes from 19 to 29 percent to 0 in the four scenes I measured, with the 60 FPS scenes at about 60 and U3 tail-sully 38 -> 53 FPS, U1 chase 54 -> 59 FPS on a loaded PC. The assertion repro (8 ms GPU lag, 40 s, fresh instance): 5 of 8 runs without the fix, 0 of 24 with this version. Tables and the limits are in the description.
